title: Control Board Fault
shortDescription: The electronic control has detected an internal fault.
fullDescription:
F1 on a Thermador microwave indicates a failure in the main control board — often the result of a power surge, age-related capacitor failure, or firmware lock-up. The control ceases function to prevent unsafe operation.

A full power reset (breaker off 10 minutes) occasionally clears transient errors. Persistent F1 requires replacing the control board.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker 10 minutes, restore power.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: Order matching control board by model; swap with unit unplugged.

whenToCallPro: Built-in microwaves are heavy and trim-kit installed — pro recommended.

faq.q: Can I order parts directly from Thermador?
faq.a: Yes — or use authorized BSH parts distributors.

title: Touch Keypad Stuck
shortDescription: A touch key appears continuously pressed.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the capacitive keypad has reported a key held for longer than the lockout timer. Cleaning product residue, a cracked overlay, or keypad failure are common causes.

Clean and dry the keypad area first. If fault persists, the keypad/membrane or control interface needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Clean keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with dry cloth, then slightly damp cloth. Avoid sprays.

whenToCallPro: If accessing the keypad requires removing the built-in trim.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F2 keypad error fix

faq.a: No — liquid can seep under buttons. Use only a lightly damp cloth.

title: Door Switch Circuit Error
shortDescription: Door interlock switches are not reporting expected states.
fullDescription:
F3 means the primary and secondary door interlock switches are out of sequence — one says door open, another says closed. This is a critical safety system and must not be bypassed.

Interlocks ensure the magnetron cannot energize with the door open. A misaligned door, broken latch, or failed switch typically causes F3.
symptoms: Will not start even with door closed

fixSteps.title: Inspect door fit
fixSteps.instruction: Door should close flush without rubbing.

fixSteps.title: Test switches
fixSteps.instruction: Unplugged, measure continuity at interlocks while closing door.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch set
fixSteps.instruction: Replace all three switches together for reliability.

whenToCallPro: If comfortable with high-voltage safety, DIY is OK — microwave capacitors hold lethal charge.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F3 door switch fix

title: Humidity Sensor Error
shortDescription: The sensor-cook humidity sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
F4 occurs on Thermador microwaves with sensor cook features when the humidity/steam sensor reports invalid readings at the start of a cycle. The sensor is located in the exhaust vent area.

Grease buildup on the sensor element is the common cause. Clean the vent area and sensor carefully without liquid ingress.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents
fixSteps.instruction: Remove vent cover and clean sensor area with degreaser wipe.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, install replacement humidity sensor.

whenToCallPro: Only if you cannot access the sensor without removing the microwave.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F4 humidity sensor fix

faq.a: Yes — F4 only affects sensor cook; manual cook still works.

title: Cavity Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The oven cavity thermistor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the cavity temperature sensor (used for convection or combination modes) is reading out of range. Without this sensor, convection cooking is disabled.

The thermistor is located on the rear wall of the cavity. Replacement is straightforward once the microwave is accessed from the rear.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat thermistor connector at control board.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Room-temp resistance should match service sheet (~10kΩ).

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor on rear cavity wall.

whenToCallPro: If microwave is a built-in combo unit that's difficult to remove.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F5 cavity sensor fix

faq.q: Is the cavity sensor the same as humidity sensor?
faq.a: No — humidity sensor is in the vent; cavity thermistor is on the rear wall.

title: Magnetron Fault
shortDescription: The magnetron is not generating microwaves correctly.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates magnetron failure — either no microwave output, excessive current draw, or overheat protection tripped. The magnetron is the high-voltage tube that generates cooking microwaves.

This repair involves the high-voltage capacitor which can store lethal charges even when unplugged. Professional service strongly recommended.
symptoms: Microwave runs but does not heat food

fixSteps.title: Water test first
fixSteps.instruction: Before opening, confirm no heating with 1 cup water for 2 min.

fixSteps.title: Call pro
fixSteps.instruction: Magnetron replacement requires HV capacitor discharge.

fixSteps.title: Replace magnetron
fixSteps.instruction: Tech discharges capacitor, installs new magnetron, checks HV diode.

whenToCallPro: Always — HV capacitor holds lethal charge. Do not DIY.

faq.q: Is repair worth it vs replacement?
faq.a: On built-ins yes — replacement microwaves cost $1500+; magnetron repair often $500-$700.

title: Cooling Fan Failure
shortDescription: The magnetron cooling fan has stopped.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates the cooling fan that blows air across the magnetron has failed or is blocked. Without airflow, the magnetron overheats and fails prematurely. The microwave disables heating until the fan is functional.

Dust accumulation on fan blades and bearing failure are the leading causes.

fixSteps.title: Listen for fan
fixSteps.instruction: Start a 30s cook — fan should run. If silent, confirm F7.

fixSteps.title: Clean fan
fixSteps.instruction: After discharge by a tech, clean blade and bearings.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan motor and harness.

whenToCallPro: Strongly — fan is usually near HV capacitor.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F7 cooling fan fix

faq.a: No. The magnetron will overheat and fail.

title: Turntable Motor Fault
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the turntable motor is not operating. While not a safety fault, uneven cooking will result. The motor is a small synchronous motor under the cavity floor.

A stuck turntable coupler or broken drive cup is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Check coupler
fixSteps.instruction: Remove glass tray and check plastic drive coupler for cracks.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Access under-cavity; measure motor winding resistance.

whenToCallPro: If motor access requires removing built-in microwave.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F8 turntable motor fix

faq.a: Yes but rotate food manually for even cooking.

title: High-Voltage Transformer Fault
shortDescription: HV transformer overcurrent or open detected.
fullDescription:
F9 signals a fault in the high-voltage transformer feeding the magnetron. The transformer steps line voltage up to ~2000V for magnetron operation. Failure manifests as overcurrent, open primary, or shorted secondary.

This is strictly professional repair — HV transformers and capacitors can deliver fatal shocks. Do not open the cover.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F9 high voltage fix

faq.a: Yes if under the original BSH warranty period (typically 2 years).

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Loss of communication between user interface and relay board.
fullDescription:
F10 indicates the UI control and the relay/power board are not communicating. On combination microwave-ovens (Thermador MC series), these are often separate boards connected by a ribbon cable.

Check cable seating first. Replacement is straightforward but access can require removing the microwave from cabinetry.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Access UI and reseat communication ribbon.

whenToCallPro: Built-in combo units are heavy and trim-installed — pro strongly recommended.
videoSearchQuery: Thermador microwave F10 communication error fix

faq.q: Will the oven function without microwave?
faq.a: On combo units, typically yes — but verify with service tech.
